text:
B: Hello! Oh, it's you, I was hoping I'd get you! I'm Chiamaka, in Leeds.
A: Oh, hello, love! Joanne, Gosport. Were you really? That's ever so nice of you.
B: Yes! Your picture, with the lighthouse and the little blanket on the settee, I said you look like the sweet ladies who bring biscuits onto the ward.
A: Ha! Well, I'm not a biscuit lady, I'm a cake lady. Victoria sponge, for birthdays. Sorry, are you a nurse, love? I saw your top.
B: Doctor. Acute medicine. I've just done four nights, so excuse my face.
A: Oh, you poor thing, you must be shattered. You look lovely, though, honestly, you've got such a smile.
B: Stop, you'll make me cry, I'm too tired for compliments! What do you do, Joanne?
A: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. Eleven years. Erm, I do the prep, serve at lunch, wash up, all that. I know all the little ones, which ones have allergies and that. I'm a bit like you, really, only with fish fingers instead of patients.
B: No, that's important! Allergies? That's life and death, that's basically medicine.
A: Oh, I don't know about that, but thank you. Erm, can I ask you something? You can say no.
B: Go on, everybody asks me things. My whole family WhatsApp.
A: It's my knees, and my chest. I've got arthritis and asthma, and the cold mornings, I'm sort of wheezing by the time I get to work. I don't like to bother the GP, they're so busy, but I've had a couple of days off lately and I feel awful letting the cook down.
B: Okay, listen to me, love. You are not bothering anybody. If your asthma's worse in the cold and you're needing your inhaler more, that's exactly what the asthma review is for, they might change what you're on. And ask about the knees too, there's physio, there's things. And please don't feel guilty about sick days. You're allowed to be a person.
A: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm going a bit wobbly. That's very kind. Thank you.
B: No sorry! I mean it. Book the review.
A: I will. I'll tell my sister you said, she's always on at me. Erm, anyway, what do you do when you're not at the hospital?
B: Church choir! I'm an alto. We've got a big Easter service coming up and we've been practising every week. And Love Island, I won't lie to you.
A: Oh, I watch Strictly with my sister on the phone, we score them ourselves. She's ever so harsh.
B: I love that! On the phone together, that's so cute.
A: Well, she's ten minutes away, but we like our own settees. Do you have a family up there?
B: My partner, Tunde, and my cousin's staying with us, she's doing nursing. She finishes the milk every single day.
A: Ha! My cat does that with his food, leaves me nothing but a dirty bowl. Biscuit. He's elderly, bless him.
B: Biscuit! That's such a good name. Of course you have a cat called Biscuit.
A: I don't know if that's very interesting, me going on about the cat.
B: It is, it's my favourite part so far!
